body: As this section has demonstrated, ANCSA has had a profound and altogether unique hand in shaping the lives of Alaska Natives, and the very political economy of the state. ANCSA was, in implementation and effect, a social experiment meant to expedite the assimilation of Native people into Western society, while simultaneously freeing up disputed lands for development and resource extraction.

Further, and from the very beginning of U.S. settler expansion into Alaska, Native people have been trying to protect their access and capacity to maintain traditional subsistence food practices. However, rather than ameliorate these concerns by directly addressing them, ANCSA failed to implement a satisfactory subsistence policy, allowing instead the concerns of settler interests to dictate Native people’s access to their foods.
